status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: Waymo temporarily paused service in response to the disruption. This demonstrates a mechanism to restrict unwanted fleet behaviour. It does not establish that every vehicle or traffic consequence was immediately resolved.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: During the outage, correlated requests for remote confirmation exceeded timely response capacity and vehicle delays contributed to congestion. The autonomy and assistance system did not maintain appropriate fleet operation under this adverse condition. It is not assigned sole responsibility for citywide gridlock.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence exposed an operational capacity boundary in a distributed autonomy-and-remote-assistance system under correlated infrastructure failure. The evidence supports service degradation, but does not establish that Waymo caused the citywide gridlock or that a selectable VIGIL failure invariant is satisfied. Correlated workload, delayed confirmation, service pause and proposed fleet/protocol changes remain separate resolved-no-mapping components. A conservative local response can overload shared capacity without proving a defined class trigger or citywide causation.
conclusion_change.new: The outage exposed a shared remote-assistance capacity limit and degraded fleet operation. A service pause is a supported mitigation. The external findings do not assign citywide causation or force a taxonomy classification.
